Leviathan's Thematic Pillar Spotlight: Defense Supercycle(3)(10)

Defense Supercycle anchors the holdco in the two sleeves that are long the geopolitical cycle: physical-layer effectors and the semiconductor / AI stack beneath them
Weapons: cash-generative defense opex — munitions, autonomy, directed energy and counter-drone demand pulled by NATO's 5%-of-GDP pledge and US replenishment budgets

Spotlight: Saronic

Investment in a leading autonomous naval-surface-vessel platform scaling under the US Navy's Replicator programme
Saronic
$9.25B
entry post-money valuation (Series D, Mar-26)
$70M
LPEH check — largest position in the holdco (9.3% of committed capital)
  • Naval autonomy is among the fastest-growing defense budget lines; the company's 2025 revenue scaled roughly 15x year-on-year

  • Ownership kept deliberately small (0.8%) given the late entry mark; value creation comes from programme-of-record wins and a public-market exit window

Returns are single-terminal-exit illustrations: proceeds = check × (1 + CAGR)^hold × retention, with fees charged on committed capital over the full hold and a whole-fund European waterfall with no GP catch-up. IRRs are therefore annualised multiples, not cash-flow IRRs, and will differ from realised figures once capital is drawn and distributed over time.

Summary of Key Terms

Key TermsDescription
VehicleLeviathan Core Private Equity Holdco: a $750M holding company owning three sub-vehicles, modelled on a committed-capital basis(1)
Sub-vehiclesDefense (Weapons sleeve, $300M) · IQT Semi / AI (IQT-mirror sleeve, $250M) · Consumer Discretionary (Consumer / Value sleeve, $200M)
Hold periods5 / 7 / 10 years modelled; the 7-year vehicle is the recommended underwriting case
Follow-on reserve of $25M within the IQT sleeve, steered pro-rata to Substrate, EUV Tech and EdgeCortix
Dilution / retention(5)Ownership retained at short / mid / long hold — IQT 85% / 78% / 68%; Weapons 92% / 88% / 82%; Consumer 90% / 84% / 75%
Scenario weights(2)Base / Bull / Bear / TSMC-Shock = 45% / 20% / 20% / 15%
TSMC-Shock CAGRs for the IQT sleeve are derived from a five-axis strategic score (China-race criticality, Taiwan insulation, government embeddedness, CFIUS-clean sovereignty, chokepoint leverage)
BenchmarksS&P 500 9.0%, Nasdaq-100 13.0%, Defense+Semis thematic basket 15.0% forward (50/50 ITA/SOXX, tempered from a ~26% trailing five-year blend)
Reference currencyUSD; all figures in USD millions unless noted

CostsFeesTerms applied in the model
Ongoing costsManagement fee2.0% per annum of committed capital, charged over the full hold
Preferred return8% per annum, compounded, returned to LPs before any carry
Incidental costsCarried interest20% of profits above the preferred return; Whole-fund European, no GP catch-up
Not modelledOrganisational, transaction and secondary-access costsExcluded; a feeder or SPV wrapper for access-constrained names would add a layer of cost not reflected here

The sub-vehicle figures on pages 1 and 4 apply the same fee, preferred-return and carry terms to each sleeve on a stand-alone basis. The holdco figures net the three sleeves under a single waterfall, so strong sleeves offset weak ones before carry is charged; the difference is reported on the Sleeve Economics tab of the model as the cross-sleeve netting effect.

Note: The information above is a summary of the terms as modelled only and is qualified in its entirety by the governing documents of any vehicle ultimately formed. Capitalised terms not defined have the meanings given in the model's Read Me tab.

Endnotes

Note: All figures presented are as of 22-Sep-2026 unless otherwise indicated and are outputs of the Leviathan Core PE Holdco model, v3 optimisation pass dated 02-Oct-2026. “LPEH”, “the holdco” and “the vehicle” refer to Leviathan Core Private Equity Holdco. Leviathan runs four vehicles (~$1.5B AUM in total); this fact sheet covers only the core PE holdco and its three sub-vehicles.

(1)Committed-capital basis. Paid-in capital is assumed fully drawn at inception, so Net DPI equals Net MOIC and RVPI is zero at exit (TVPI = DPI).

(2)“Expected” figures are probability-weighted across the four scenarios (Base / Bull / Bear / TSMC-Shock = 45% / 20% / 20% / 15%). Each line of the net waterfall is weighted separately and ratios are then derived from the weighted net proceeds, so Expected net figures are the expected value of LP proceeds rather than the waterfall applied to expected gross proceeds. Headline figures use the 7-year hold.

(3)The sub-vehicle and investment examples presented reflect the modelled target book as of 22-Sep-2026. They are shown to illustrate the vehicle's themes and are not a representation that any position will be acquired on the modelled terms. Several names require secondary, tender, cornerstone or block access that has not been secured.

(4)Net returns are after a 2.0% management fee on committed capital over the full hold, an 8% compounded preferred return and 20% carried interest under a whole-fund European waterfall with no GP catch-up. Gross and net IRRs are annualised multiples ((proceeds / capital)^(1/hold) − 1), not cash-flow IRRs; a wipe-out is shown as −100%.

(5)Retention is the share of entry ownership kept after follow-on dilution, applied to exit proceeds, and is set per sleeve and per hold.

(6)“Sector Breakdown” groups holdings into Leviathan's ten thematic sectors by committed check. Classifications are made in Leviathan's sole discretion; different criteria could result in materially different classifications.

(7)“Regional Breakdown” is by principal place of business. DefendEye (US HQ, Polish manufacturing, EU cap table) is classified North America. Allied-nation names (EdgeCortix, Diraq) are minority-only positions.

(8)“Stage & Liquidity Breakdown” reflects the entry route: listed shares, pre-IPO / IPO-track names, late-stage private rounds, tenders and secondaries, growth-stage primaries, and seed / early rounds.

(9)Represents LPEH's modelled committed capital of $750M; all breakdowns are percentages of that total and may not sum to 100% due to rounding.

(10)“Thematic Pillar” is selected from the drivers set out on the model's Macro Overlay tab (NATO 5%-of-GDP pledge, US munitions and autonomy budgets, classified / black-budget growth, China decoupling and CHIPS reshoring). Saronic entry mark: Series D, March 2026, $9.25B post-money; 2025 revenue of approximately $200M.

(11)Top 10 positions are the ten largest modelled checks by committed capital and are listed in descending order of check size.

Modelled returns. The model compounds a per-name CAGR over a single terminal exit; it does not model interim cash flows, recycling, credit facilities, FX, taxes or organisational expenses. Six of nine IQT-sleeve entry marks and most Weapons-sleeve marks are estimates pending primary cap-table access; two Consumer-sleeve marks (Made In Cookware, Plunge) have no market reference and Goat Group's last priced round is from June 2021. The TSMC-Shock case is a deliberately low-probability tail whose compounded CAGRs produce very large multiples by design; its weight should be kept honest.
